circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be built, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street course that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Australian Grand Prix annually alongside the Supercars Championship and various support categories. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing modifications and renaming, the track returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, situated along Baku Boulevard with a 6. 003 km lap length that ranks as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix before being officially renamed for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that has hosted the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix annually, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern venue. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various motorsport categories including endurance racing and formerly hosted touring car events, while maintaining multiple configuration options and FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has hosted Formula One racing since 1950 and has been the venue for the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The track, which also staged motor racing events before the Formula One era, remains one of the championship's longest and most challenging venues.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre temporary racing venue that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond hosting the premier motorsport series, the circuit has accommodated numerous other racing competitions including international sportscar championships and various North American touring series over the years.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in the Jiading district hosts China's premier motorsport events, most notably the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. In addition to the Formula One race, the venue began accommodating electric racing competitions from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in England between the Northamptonshire settlements of Silverstone and Whittlebury, has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades, the grand prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, which also serves as a venue for the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months following October 1985 groundbreaking, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track established in 1922 that ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues. It hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, making it one of the few circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar, and earns its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its distinctive layout of extended straights and fast-cornering sections.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts major international racing events. The track, with a capacity of 155,000 spectators, is particularly renowned for staging Formula One grands prix and Japanese Super Formula races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track positioned in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the famous hotel and casino district along Las Vegas Boulevard. The course weaves past iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two brothers, Ricardo and Pedro, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, following a prior stint that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Created by specialist track designers for the 2022 Formula One season, the venue primarily hosts the Miami Grand Prix, though a modified configuration has been adapted for electric racing series from 2025-26 onwards.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, winding around Monaco's harbor. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is popularly known as Monte Carlo since the majority of the track traverses that particular district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. The track's distinctive character comes from its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, earning it the affectionate nickname "Roller coaster in the Dunes" among Formula One enthusiasts.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, this 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The anticlockwise layout hosts major international racing events and features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to another Brazilian motorsporting icon.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has served as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its introduction to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The track also began hosting an international electric racing championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary road course located around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating sections through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue located in Montmeló near Barcelona, designed as a versatile circuit featuring extended straights and diverse corner configurations. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP, and endurance racing competitions, while previously welcoming various other series ranging from rallycross to IndyCar racing.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams, competing under Thailand's flag in Formula One.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he secured consecutive world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One title and a world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for Mercedes, establishing a record as the sport's youngest champion. Since joining the grid in 2025, he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto competes in Formula One, currently racing for the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. Previously with Mercedes, he achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine racing driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian racer who serves as a reserve driver for Haas in Formula One, having made seven Grand Prix appearances across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Beyond his Formula One commitments, he races in endurance competitions, including the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing and the Asian Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with AF Corse.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver competing in Formula One for Alpine, previously secured victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while racing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: A British driver competing for Ferrari, Hamilton shares the record for seven world championship titles with Schumacher while holding multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his motorsport career. Beyond his F1 commitments, he achieved a significant milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while racing for the Maranello-based team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR duties with Trackhouse Racing. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate periods between 2014 and 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship competing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver who last drove for Haas in Formula One. The driver achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac. Throughout his 15-season career, he has claimed six Grand Prix victories and finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12 seasons in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who recently concluded his Formula One tenure spanning 2023 and 2024. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously competed in IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One driving for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, competed as a full-time Formula One competitor for five seasons starting in 2021 before transitioning to a reserve role for Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has claimed four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the series across 2022-2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. The Chinese driver currently supports the American team in a developmental capacity while remaining an active part of the paddock.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021, this team competed under the Alpine banner as Renault's official works squad, having previously raced as Renault F1 Team. The rebranding aimed to highlight Renault's Alpine sports car division, though the team maintained its factory status throughout its tenure before Renault's Formula One exit concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has been involved in Formula One through multiple team entities, with the current operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, having participated in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the championship's seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas Formula LLC is an American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas in 2014 and launched into competition in 2016. The outfit is currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over the position in early 2024 following Guenther Steiner's departure after leading the team since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing outfit established in 1970, Sauber competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor, achieving notable success in endurance racing including a Le Mans victory in 1989. The team underwent several transformations during its three-decade Formula One tenure before ceasing operations in 2025 as the sport's fourth-most experienced constructor by race count, at which point Audi acquired its operations to establish their own factory team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under title sponsorship. The team operates as part of the wider McLaren Group and is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One continuously since 1954 in various capacities, most prominently as a team owner and engine supplier. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos since January 2022, with equal stakes among all three parties. The team carries the historic "Silver Arrows" designation, synonymous with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operational facilities in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor unit.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's secondary racing outfit in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England, owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005 and managed by Christian Horner until 2025, the team is now led by Laurent Mekies following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of the sport's established operations.
